definitions.explanation: Poetry written in classical Chinese, including works by Chinese poets and poems composed in classical Chinese by Japanese poets. A major literary tradition studied in Japanese education.

examples.japanese: {漢詩|かんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{暗唱|あんしょう}する→暗唱する：26776_anshousuru⟧。
examples.english: I recite Chinese poetry from memory.

examples.japanese: ⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{漢詩|かんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}った→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: I studied Chinese poetry in high school Japanese class.

examples.japanese: {李白|りはく}や{杜甫|とほ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{漢詩|かんし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{広|ひろ}く→広い：00704_hiroi⟧⟦{親|した}しまれている→親しむ：14139_shitashimu⟧。
examples.english: The Chinese poetry of Li Bai and Du Fu is widely appreciated in Japan as well.

notes:
USAGE:
{漢詩|かんし} is part of the Japanese school curriculum and is studied in ⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧ (Japanese language) class, not as a foreign language. Classical Chinese poems are read using {訓読|くんどく}み (Japanese reading of Chinese text), which rearranges the word order and adds Japanese grammatical particles.

Japanese scholars and poets also composed their own {漢詩|かんし} throughout history, particularly during the Heian and Edo periods.

Do not confuse with the homophone ⟦{監視|かんし}→監視：05521_kanshi⟧ (surveillance), which uses different kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漢詩|かんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧: to compose Chinese poetry
- {漢詩|かんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧: to read Chinese poetry
- {唐|とう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{漢詩|かんし}: Tang dynasty Chinese poetry
